sections.markdown:
## C — Health, vehicle checks and basic driving

FACT_ID: sec04-F01 | anchor: A01
Even minor health problems such as a cold, stiff neck, cough or sore leg can hurt your driving, and conditions like epilepsy, diabetes or heart trouble can make driving unsafe, so ask your doctor if unsure. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec04-F02 | anchor: A01
Strong emotions such as worry, excitement, fear or anger can degrade your driving, and you should never give in to road rage. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec04-F03 | anchor: A01
Distraction is the leading cause of driver error, defined as anything that pulls your attention from driving, even for a moment. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec04-F04 | anchor: A01
Before you set off, adjust your seat, mirrors, radio and temperature, secure loose items, and make sure everyone, especially children, is in an age-appropriate restraint. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec04-F05 | anchor: A01
Avoid distraction from your phone, passengers, children or rubbernecking, which means staring at something of interest, and pull over safely to handle anything urgent. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec04-F06 | anchor: A01
Drivers are responsible for keeping their vehicle safe; a poorly maintained car costs more, can break down or crash, and can earn you a citation. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec04-F07 | anchor: A01
If the brakes seem wrong, have a mechanic check them right away, and make sure turn signals, brake lights, tail lights and headlights all work. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec04-F08 | anchor: A01
Replace a damaged windshield and worn wiper blades, keep the glass clean inside and out with the washer tank full, and clear snow, ice or frost from every window. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec04-F09 | anchor: A01
Worn or bald tires lengthen stopping distance, make turning harder, invite hydroplaning on wet roads and raise the chance of a flat. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec04-F10 | anchor: A01
Low tire pressure and unbalanced wheels wear tires faster, cut fuel economy and make steering and stopping harder; a bouncing car, shaking wheel or pull to one side means get the tires checked. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec04-F11 | anchor: A01
Have a mechanic look at the steering if the car is hard to turn, and at the suspension if it bounces too much or keeps bouncing after a bump or a stop. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec04-F12 | anchor: A01
Exhaust fumes from a leak can kill very quickly, so never run the engine in a garage or sit in a running car without a window open. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec04-F13 | anchor: A01
A poorly tuned engine may lose power, fail to start, waste fuel, pollute and stall in traffic; the horn should also be checked regularly. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec04-F14 | anchor: A01
Set the driver-side mirror with your head against the left window so the side of the car is barely visible at the left edge of the mirror. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec04-F15 | anchor: A01
Set the passenger-side mirror with your head centered under the inside rearview mirror, or just above the center console, so the side of the car just shows at the right edge. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec04-F16 | anchor: A01
Remove loose objects from the rear shelf and back seat that could hurt someone in a sudden stop, and from the floor where they could roll under the pedals. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec04-F17 | anchor: A01
Adjust the head restraint so it touches the back of your head. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec04-F18 | anchor: A01
Whatever the make or model, keep your right foot on the brake when starting the vehicle, then check the indicator lights and gauges for maintenance warnings. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec04-F19 | anchor: A01
To pull away, find a safe path, check for traffic and pedestrians to the sides and rear, signal, then press the accelerator gently with the ball of your foot while your heel rests on the floor. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec04-F20 | anchor: A01
To stop, check your mirrors for traffic behind, move your foot from the accelerator to the brake, and press with steady pressure until the vehicle stops. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec04-F21 | anchor: A01
Always turn the steering wheel toward the direction you want the vehicle to go, whether moving forward or backing up. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec04-F22 | anchor: A01
For best control, hold the outside of the wheel on opposite sides at the 3 and 9 o'clock or the 4 and 8 o'clock positions. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec04-F23 | anchor: A01
Grip the wheel firmly but gently with your fingers rather than your palms, keep your thumbs up along the face of the wheel, and never hold the inside of the rim while turning. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0009]
